NWS storm survey found the path of an EF1 tornado that began in the vicinity of Porter Ridge High School. Tree branches were broken and a free-standing light pole was  broken off at the base. The fence around the schools tennis court was also blown over and two storage buildings collapsed nearby. The tornado moved northeast   across Ridge Road, where a house under construction was heavily damaged, presumably due to air rushing in via window and garage door openings, which lifted off part of the roof. Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped along Friendship Baptist Church Rd. Minor structural damage occurred to a house in the Benton Acres neighborhood. The tornado continued northeast to Lawyers Rd just west of US 601, snapping several hundred yards of wooden power poles, while causing little damage to adjacent homes. The tornado apparently dissipated at this location.

Multiple sources reported flash flooding developed on the north side of Lenoir after 2 to 4 inches of rain fell over the area in less than two hours. The main impacts were to Blair Fork and its tributaries. Blair Fork overflowed its bans and inundated multiple roads, including Main St NW and Valway Rd, where water was up to car doors. Multiple water rescues were reported along Blair Fork. Water from a tributary inundated  portions of Indian Grave Rd and Bill Tuttle Rd, where water entered a mobile home. Zacks Fork Creek also reportedly overflowed its banks onto a section of Zacks Fork Rd.

Stream gauges and the media reported flash flooding developed across south Charlotte after 2.5 to 5 inches of rain fell across the area due to slow-moving, repeating thunderstorms. Most of the major streams in this part of the city overflowed their banks and inundated adjacent roads, greenways, and residential yards, including Little Hope Creek, Edwards Branch, and Little Sugar Creek. The most significant flooding occurred along Steele Creek in the Steele Creek community, which inundated a mobile home park. Multiple manufactured homes were inundated in this area, and multiple vehicles were largely subsumed in water. Around 30 swift water rescues occurred throughout the city during the event, with most of these occurring in the mobile home park. Thirteen people were also rescued from their vehicles near Freedom Park (Little Sugar Creek). McMullen Creek also experienced severe flooding, with water entering the crawl spaces of some homes and cutting off access to others.

Although heavy rain had ended across the Charlotte area by late evening, flooding persisted along multiple streams in the south Charlotte area as flows remained elevated due to the torrential rainfall that fell earlier in the evening. All streams receded to their banks shortly after midnight.

Numerous roads were flooded and/or closed due to poor drainage and stream flooding across the southern part of the county. Flooded roads included Tom Starnes, Austin, Little Sleepy Hollow, Medlin, Bruce Thomas, portions of highway 522, Doster, and White Store Rd.

Around 6 inches of water flowed over highway 70 due to flooding along the Catawba River. Catawba River Rd was also flooded in the western part of the county. Also, Crooked Creek flooded Crooked Creek Rd in the western part of the county.
Flooding along Caney Fork resulted in the closing of Helen Zachary Rd and Caney Fork Rd.

Water from the Pigeon River flooded Max Thompson Rd, five miles west southwest of Canton, and Thickety Rd in Clyde. Also, Beaver Run Rd was closed after a small earthen dam gave way on Beaverdam Creek.

Several streams flooded across eastern portions of the county when up to 10 inches of rain fell in about a 24 hour period. Unofficial reports of up to 16 inches of rain were received. The South Toe River flooded portions of highway 80. Some streets were closed in Micaville due to urban flooding. A campground was flooded when the South Toe flooded just north of Celo. All of the camp sites were flooded, as were some outdoor facilities.

Water from the Linville River, Shooks Creek, and Sandy Bar covered Parks Dr 12.5 miles west northwest of Morganton. Also, the Johns River flooded part of Johns River Rd 7.5 miles north northwest of town. In addition, Bost Rd was closed near its intersection with Spainhour Rd due to flooding on Warrior Fork.
Wilson Creek flooded Brown Mountain Beach Rd about 10 miles west of Lenoir, while the Johns River flooded a portion of Playmore Beach Rd in the same general area.
Pine Ave and Moose St were inpassable due to flooding along Beaverdam Creek. Very high water was reported at an apartment complex in this same area.

A 25 foot section of East 1st St in Newton was washed out by water from Snow Hill Creek. Also, Rocky Ford Rd was closed due to flooding along the South Fork River. A section of Little Rd was washed out near the intersection of Albert Dr.

Severe flash flooding developed along Briar Creek in east Charlotte.  Numerous cars were submerged on Independence Bvd, with some rescues required. Numerous evacuations were required of homes and apartments along the creek, as water entered dozens of structures. Uninsured losses included major damage to 147 homes and 1 business. Affected roads included Dunlavin Way, Harbinger Ct, Chantilly Lane, Cavalier Ct, and Dolphin Lane. Several houses and one apartment complex on these streets were condemned by the city.

Emergency manager reported flash flooding developed across portions of central and southern Rabun County after 4 to 5.5 inches of rain fell across the area in around 24 hours, with around half of that falling in around six hours during the morning of the 10th. Impacts began with an embankment failure along Highway 76 just west of Clayton, where a lane of the highway was covered and a vehicle briefly trapped. Stekoa Creek overflowed its banks just south of Clayton, with water inundating Rickman Airfield Rd. Chechero Creek also  overflowed onto Country Club Dr near Highway 76. Additionally, minor flooding was reported in spots along Tiger Creek from the headwaters to its confluence with the Tallulah River. Portions of Old Highway 441 were inundated, including at Shady Lane.
Two trees were blown down.
Trees were blown down on Interstate 77 near exit 42.
Power poles were snapped and large trees blown down on Charlotte Highway northwest of Mooresville. Trees were also blown down on West Park Ave near Beam Dr.
Large tree limbs were blown down on Dogwood Dr.

Trees were blown down on Carpenters Grove Church Rd about 5 miles north of Fallston. Two trees fell on a mobile home on highway 18 in the Bellwood community, and the roof was blown off a barn in the same area.
Two trees were blown down.
Trees were blown down in the Cornelia area.
A tree and power lines were blown down south of Harmony.
Numerous trees were blown down by two thunderstorms across the northern part of the county.
Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted, as well as large limbs blown down.
Hail reported at Victoria Bryant State Park.
Trees were blown down.
Several reports of large hail ranging from quarter size to golf ball size were received from the west side of Greenville.
Multiple power lines were blown down in and around Bowman. Also, a large tree fell on a home on Winston Dr and another large tree was blown over on Church St.

GSP ASOS measured a wind gust of 56 knots, or 64 mph. The roofs of a barn and outbuilding were blown off, siding and shingles were torn off a house, and numerous trees were blown down. One of the trees fell on a garage on Apple Valley Rd in Reidville.
Hail reported on Wade Hampton Blvd.
Large tree limbs blown down on Pearson Rd.
Numerous trees were blown down across the county. A roof was blown off a building on the west side of Gaffney.
Numerous trees blown down across the northern part of Union County. Areas west of Lockhart were especially hard hit.
Hail was reported at the intersection of highway 9 and highway 18.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down, especially across the western and northern sections of the county.
Trees were blown down in the Carlisle area.
Hail was reported near Lake Keowee.
Large tree limbs were blown down on Perimeter Rd.
Trees were blown down in the Salem area.

Part of the roof was blown off a home on Moorehead Rd, with fallen trees causing damage to several other homes in the area. Several power poles were blown down on Millwee Creek Rd and a barn was destroyed on Autun Rd.
Trees were blown down on Wilson Rd.
Large limbs were blown down.
Large tree limbs and the top of a tree were blown out in the area around Bracketts Cedar Park. A tree was also blown down on highway 10 about 3 miles north of Polkville.
Reported on highway 182.
Power lines were blown down on Eaglewood Rd and 2 trees were downed, blocking a lane of traffic, on Martin Hills Rd.
A tree and power lines were blown down highway 34 just southeast of the city.
Trees were blown down on McKenzie Rd, Kinard Rd, and Epworth Camp Rd.
Large tree limbs were blown down.
Large tree limbs were blown down on Perth Rd.
Several trees were blown down onto power lines in the Fort Lawn area.

This tornado touched down near Oak Crest Dr in the Reed Creek community in extreme northeast Hart County, then skipped across Lake Hartwell before tracking into extreme western Anderson County in South Carolina. The intermittent damage path was mainly limited to downed trees and power lines, although some minor structural damage was noted near Reed Creek.

This tornado touched down in Hart County, Georgia before skipping  across Lake Hartwell and into extreme western Anderson County. The tornado then moved into Oconee County. The intermittent damage path was mainly limited to downed trees and power lines in Anderson County.

This tornado moved into Oconee County from Pickens County. It then tracked into western Pickens County. The intermittent damage path was mainly limited to downed trees and power lines in Oconee County.

This tornado tracked from Oconee County into extreme western Pickens County. The tornado lifted just after crossing the campus of Clemson University. The intermittent damage path was mainly limited to downed trees and power lines, although some minor structural damage was noted, especially on the Clemson campus near Memorial Stadium. Some trees and large limbs fell on and damaged automobiles in the Clemson area.
Trees blown onto power lines on highway 137.
Trees and large limbs blown onto power lines.
Winds gusting from 35 to 45 mph across the foothills resulted in a few downed trees across Burke County, with one tree falling on a home in Valdese.

The tornado touched down in rural, southern Greenville County. As it crossed Davis and Richey Roads, about 5 miles east of Pelzer, it destroyed a garage, removed shingles from roofs and uprooted large trees. The tornado continued north into Moonville where it blew down more trees. It then lifted about nine miles south of Greenville.

A tornado touched down near highway 187 and Mt. Tabor road where a home was damaged and a tree fell on a mobile home. The tornado continued to the north, eventually moving into Pickens County. Numerous large trees were snapped off on a ridge very close to the Pickens/Anderson County line, where wind speeds were estimated at close to 120 mph, earning the tornado an EF2 rating.

A tornado damage path extended from northwest Anderson County, into extreme southern Pickens County, affecting the research area on the south side of the Clemson University campus.  Damage was limited to downed trees and power lines. Numerous large trees were snapped off on a ridge very close to the Pickens, Anderson County line, where wind speeds were estimated at close to 120 mph, earning the tornado an EF2 rating.
A tree was blown down on highway 97 near Chester, and another along Mountain Lakes Rd.

Numerous roads were closed, mainly due to stream flooding from Harrisburg to Concord to Mount Pleasant. Several homes received significant damage due to floodwater, with Harrisburg being the hardest hit. Closed roads included highway 73 near Dutch Rd, Red Bird Cir, Morehead Rd from highway 29 to highway 49, Miami Church Rd, Stough Rd near Marlboro Dr, Bowman Barrier Rd, Zion Church Rd at Flowes Store Rd, Pharr Mill Rd at Sequoia Hills Dr, and a portion of highway 200.

Flooding began with closing of highway 152 and Atwell Rd in the southwest part of the county. Flooding quickly expanded to Salisbury and the Kannapolis area, with vehicles trapped in flood water on Old Concord Rd near Salisbury. A rest home was evacuated on Lush Dr in Salisbury when water began entering the building. Two families required rescue when their homes were flooded with at least a foot of water from Cane Creek near the intersection of Faith Rd and Byrd Rd. At least one motorist required rescue when water from Town Creek overflowed East Innes St at I-85. Floodwater in this area was several feet deep, causing damage to quite a few businesses. Poor drainage also caused deep standing water to form on N Long St, where at least one vehicle was submerged. By mid-morning numerous rescues were underway on Old Beatty Ford Rd in the Landis, Kannapolis area.

Numerous streets and roads were closed in and around Kannapolis, due to flooding streams and poor drainage. Evacuations were necessary at a rest home on Pine St. Closed roads included Sloop Rd, Trinity Church Rd, Dogwood Bvd, Dakota St, Lane St, Oakwood Ave, South Little Texas Rd, Mallard Point Rd, and East 1st St. At least 14 swift water rescues were necessary. Approximately 70 buildings were damaged by floodwater across Cabarrus County.

Although flash flooding ended across the area by mid-morning, stream levels remained elevated, and in some cases continued to slowly rise into the afternoon hours. In fact, the South Fork River did not crest until mid-evening. Numerous roads remained closed through the day.

Although flash flooding ended across the area by mid-morning, stream levels remained elevated, and in some cases continued to slowly rise into the afternoon hours. Numerous roads remained closed through the day.
NWS employee reported dime to nickel size hail near the Burke County line.
Media reports multiple trees blown down along and near Providence Church Ln.
Fire marshal reported a couple of trees blown down in the Unionville area, with one tree down on a house.

A brief, weak tornado with touched down just south of Mars Hill between Interstate-26 and South Main St. It traveled for about half a mile, uprooting several trees and snapping branches before lifting near Bold Springs Dr.

A weak tornado touched down several miles east of Mars Hill, uprooting and snapping numerous trees. A path of damage was evident for a little over two miles along Paint Fork Road before disappearing into the higher terrain approaching Chestnut Mountain, just past Metcalf Creek Loop.

A weak tornado touched down along N Graham St near the intersection of Moretz Ave, where several small trees were snapped. The tornado moved northeast into a residential area, where additional large limbs were snapped. The tornado reached peak intensity of 85 mph as it crossed Atando Ave where sheet metal was peeled back off a large industrial building. Another warehouse sustained more significant roof damage with a large section of roofing removed. Several large pine trees were snapped behind the warehouse. The tornado weakened and eventually dissipated as it moved into another residential area along Drury Dr where a few small limbs were downed.

NWS employee reported multiple trees blown down on Highway 74 west of Waynesville. Utility company reported sporadic power outages due to downed trees from the Waynesville and Maggie Valley areas across Clyde and Canton.
NWS employee reported trees blown down along Highway 74 just west of Sylva.

Multiple sources reported a smattering of trees blown down across northeast Buncombe County, from the Woodfin area, across Weaverville to the Dillingham community. Several trees were down across roads, and a barn was damaged by a fallen tree near Weaverville.
NWS storm survey and emergency manager reported a few trees blow down due to downburst winds across the southeast corner of Madison County from Holcombe Branch Rd to Metcalf Creek Loop.
Spotter reported multiple trees and power lines blown down with power outages in the Fairview area.
County comms reported multiple trees blown down along Highway 70 west of Morganton.
Emergency manager reported a tree blown down on Highway 221 South. Utility company reported a tree down on power lines and causing an outage on nearby Hines Rd.
Spotter reported multiple trees blown down off Highway 115 and additional trees down on Highway 901 in the Harmony area.
Spotter reported multiple trees blown down in the Statesville area.
Spotter reported trees blown down on Highway 150, with another tree down on Main St on the west side of Salisbury.
Several sources reported multiple trees and some power lines blown down near Uptown Charlotte. Wind equipment on Bank of America stadium meaured a gust of 61 mph.

NWS storm survey found an area of straight-line wind damage in Gaffney. Damage was first observed within the city limits, where corrugated metal roof panels, wooden joists, and fascia were ripped off the front of a small business along West Frederick Street. The wind also shifted the exterior metal wall of a nearby auto parts store, causing the corner panels to buckle and separate. East of there, a large tree was uprooted next to a house between Marion Avenue and Mill Street.
NWS storm survey reported multiple trees blown down near the GSP Airport.
Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing outages along highway 178 and in the northlakes area.
Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing an outage off of Highway 107.
Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing an outage along Highway 64 west of Hendersonville.

Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing an outage along Parker Farm Rd.

Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing outages in Belmont and vicinity.
Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing an outage along Dutch Rd.
Public reported 3/4 inch hail on Cedar Hill Rd.
Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing multiple power outages between Travelers Rest and Tigerville.
Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing outages in Joanna and vicinity.
Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing an outage along Melvin Hill Rd.
Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing an outage along Hopewell Church Rd.
Public reported 3/4 inch hail near the Laurens Rd and I-385 intersection.
Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing an outage along Joe Davis Rd.
Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing an outage in the Gumlog community.
Utility company reported trees blown down on power lines and causing an outage along Luther Burton Rd.
Public reported 3/4 inch hail off Wallace Springs Rd.
Public reported multiple trees blown down in a wooded area off of Transport Pl NW.
Public reported 3/4 inch hail.
Spotter reported 3/4 inch hail in northern Mitchell County.
Heavy rain caused a mudslide to develop on a hillside that had been cleared for construction. Water and debris entered a business at the bottom of the hill, causing some damage.
A combination of gusty winds and a soaked ground resulting from very heavy rainfall caused a tree to fall on a mobile home, briefly trapping the occupant.
A combination of gusty winds and wet ground resulting from very heavy rainfall caused a tree to fall on a house, destroying a screen porch.

Elevated stream levels on Kings Creek caused a debris dam to form beneath a bridge on Old Chester Road on the York County line. The bridge pilings were damaged, eventually causing one lane of the bridge to collapse.
Turkey Creek overflowed its banks, flooding pastures and farmland with several feet of water. A driveway was also covered with up to four feet of water.
Elevated stream levels on Wolf Creek caused a debris dam to form beneath a bridge on River Road, damaging the pilings and eventually causing it to collapse.
Very heavy rainfall combined with clogged storm drains to produce deep standing water in a neighborhood on the east side of Gaffney. A couple of automobiles were submerged.

Oak Park Rd was flooded by Tools Fork Creek and Reese Roach Rd was also flooded at McConnells Highway in the same area. Old Limestone Rd was closed at Southbend Rd and Portions of highway 72 were covered with water from Stoney Fork Creek.
Heavy rain developed well ahead of the remnants of Tropical Storm Fay, resulting in flash flooding over the north-central part of the county.
Flash flooding was reported from Demorest to Mt. Airy.
Stream flooding forced closure of Bear Gap Rd about 5 miles southwest of Lakemont and Cat Gap Rd about 8 miles west northwest of Clayton.
Numerous trees down on the east side of Charlotte.
Four trees were blown down in the Cowan���s Ford Dam area.
Hail was reported on Old Mocksville Rd.
Hail was reported on Four Oaks Dr.
Hail was reported near the intersection of Youngs Gap Rd and Lindsey Loop. Large hail also caused significant damage to the apple crop in the area around Saint Pauls Rd and Old Clear Creek Rd.
Hail reported on highway 64 west of Green Hill.
Hail was reported in the Sunny View community.
Numerous reports of penny to golf ball size hail were received from the Statesville area.
Hail was reported along Middle Street in Caroleen.
Hail was reported near the intersection of highway 70 and Bethesda Rd.
Power lines were blown down on Webb Farm Rd. A tree was also blown down in Mooresboro at the same time.
Reported on Howard Cole Rd.
Hail was reported on Big Allen Rd in the Danieltown area.
Hail was reported near the intersection of highway 120 and Family Dr.
Hail was reported on highway 901 west of Union Grove.
Hail was reported on highway 150 southwest of Salisbury.
Trees were blown down on power lines on highway 52 near Saint Luke Church Rd.
Hail was reported on highway 52 near Saint Luke Church Rd.
Hail was reported on highway 72 southwest of Rock Hill.

Significant flash flooding developed along Little Sugar Creek in northeast Charlotte. Sugar Creek Rd and Tryon St were immersed by flood water, with at least one automobile submerged. Several water rescues were required in the area, with some people trapped in their homes. A homeless shelter was damaged by floodwater on N Tryon St.
Trees and power lines were blown down across roads in the southern part of the county, including Kathy Hill Rd, Whitehall Rd, and Callison Highway.

Broadcast media reported gusty winds combined with a very wet ground resulting from heavy rainfall caused a tree to fall on a house and a vehicle on Fulwer St. Another tree fell on a home on Virginia Circle. Both of these events were in the city of Anderson.
Trees were blown down.
Trees were blown down in the Tulula community and in the Stecoah community.
Trees were blown down in the Oconaluftee area.
A tree was blown down on highway 25 near Cokesbury.
A tree was blown down on highway 254 between Hodges and Cokesbury.
A tree blown down on I-26 near Enoree, and another was blown down on highway 92 near town.

This tornado developed just south of the intersection of Mount Pleasant Rd North and Gold Hill Rd, where part of the roof and southwest side wall of a barn were lifted and tossed 20 to 30 yards. The tornado continued almost due north, roughly paralleling Mount Pleasant Rd, knocking a mobile home 5-10 feet off its foundation on Gold Hill Rd. The tornado continued its intermittent track to the north toward Klutz Rd, where a barn received some minor roof damage and a large hardwood tree snapped off and destroyed a travel trailer. The south side of a barn was torn off and lifted just north of Klutz Rd, with debris scattered up to 100 yards north of the structure. The tornado lifted shortly after this damage occurred. In addition to the structural damage, quite a few trees were snapped off or uprooted along the 2.5 mile track.

Streams flooded bridges and secondary roads across the western part of the county, after 5 to 6 inches of rain fell over a period of several hours. Many roads were closed. There were also quite a few minor mudslides and trees uprooted due to saturated ground.
The combination of saturated ground from heavy rainfall and gusty winds felled a tree on Stoney Mountain Rd. The tree fell on and destroyed a porch and damaged an automobile.
Water from Clarke Creek briefly overflowed a bridge on Cox Mill Rd.
Water covered parts of Arthur Drake Rd when the Little Tennessee River overflowed its banks, flooding low lying areas.
A combination of gusty winds and saturated ground due to recent heavy rainfall caused a large tree to fall on a home on highway 25.
A large tree, apparently weakened due to strong winds from the previous day and a wet ground, fell on a home in the Duncan Park area, causing quite a bit of damage.
Gusty winds blew down a tree on East 11th St, causing damage to a home.
Gusty winds took down a tree which damaged the roof of a home at the corner of Maple and Palmer streets.
Part of a tree fell on and crushed an outbuilding at a historic homesite on Little River Rd.
A tree was blown down on Talulah Rd and another on Old Talulah Rd.
Numerous trees blown down throughout the county.
Trees were blown down in the southern part of the county.
Trees were blown down on highway 17 in Royston.
A tree was blown down on Sandy Springs Rd at Rowland.
Trees were blown down on Concord Rd and Brown Rd.
A gust of 58 mph was measured by the ASOS equipment at the Greenville-Spartanburg airport.
The metal roof was blown off a car wash on Parris Bridge Rd.
Numerous trees were blown down across the county, especially concentrated in the Gaffney and Blacksburg areas. Also, a greenhouse received major damage on Cherokee Ave.
Trees and power lines were blown down in Crouse.
Trees and power lines were blown down along highway 27 west of Lincolnton.
Several trees were blown down on roads across the county, with one tree on an automobile.
Two trees were blown down near the intersection of Bush Rd and highway 55.

Newspaper reported two trees were blown down on Charles St, with one tree bringing down a power line. Also, an outbuilding was blown off its foundation at 3rd St and Whitehead Ave. Finally, a chimney was blown off a home near 4th St and South Rowan Ave.
Two trees were blown down. One tree was blown onto a power line.
A portion of the roof and some siding was torn off a mobile home. A tree was also blown down in the same area.
Hail reported on Jameson Rd.
Hail reported at Westgate Mall.
Hail reported in the Converse Heights area.

Quite a few roads were closed due to flood water across central and northern portions of the county. Some flooding was the result of overflowing streams, while some was caused by poor drainage. Affected roads included but were not limited to Macedonia Church Rd, Antioch Church Rd at Highview Rd, Howey Bottoms Rd at Duncan Rd, and Jackson and Benton Streets in the city of Monroe.
A brief tornado touchdown was reported near the Georgia state line. This tornado occurred in conjunction with a supercell thunderstorm.

The tornado damage path began near Farmers Academy Rd, about 0.5 mile south of highway 106. The tornado crossed Red Hill School Rd, where some outbuildings were destroyed and a couple of mobile homes received minor roof damage. As the tornado continued northeast, some frame homes on highway 106 received minor roof damage. The most significant damage occurred on Crumps Bridge Rd, where one large chicken house was completely destroyed, and several others received major damage. The tornado continued to move northeast, uprooting or snapping off numerous trees as it crossed highway 145 and Greater Hope Rd. From there, the tornado began to move in a more east/northeast direction, continuing to blow down trees as it moved roughly parallel to North Clarks Creek Rd.  As the tornado crossed Hulsey Rd, roofs were blown off the wood frame addition to a mobile home and a barn. After the tornado crossed highway 17 and Pleasant Hill Circle, it continued to turn more to the right, traveling due east near the to Wilson Rd, where a mobile home was moved off its foundation, and the steel siding and some roofing material was blown off a building. The tornado continued to travel east, or even east/southeast, before lifting in the Gerrard Rd area.
Hail reported on Old Catholic Church Rd.
Hail covered the ground.
Hail reported on Clemson Blvd.
Hail reported about 1 mile north of exit 1 on I-85.
Hail reported on I-85.
Reported at Coop station.

Numerous hail reports were received in this area. Reports included penny size hail near the Lowes Motor Speedway, several quarter size hail reports in the Concord area and half dollar sie hail in Mount Pleasant.
Hail reported on the campus of UNC Charlotte.
Trees were blown down in the Harris community.
A few trees were blown down in the Franks Creek area.
Hail reportedly dented cars in the Batesville community.
Trees down across much of the county.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down throughout the county.

NWS survey found an area of tornado damage that began on Dry Rock Rd near its intersection with Andersonville Rd. (It is possible that the tornado began over Lake Hartwell.) Damage was mainly confined to uprooted or snapped trees at this point, although two mobile homes were shifted off their foundation at this location.. The most significant damage occurred just east of this location, in the Snyder Rd area. A storage shelter was destroyed in this area and a travel trailer blown off concretet blocks. Other storage shelters received signifiumerous trees were snapped off or uprooted along Snyder Rd, with trees falling on several homes. The tornado traveled east from Snyder Rd, crossing an inlet of Lake Hartwell before re-emerging in the Sandy Shores Dr area. The tornado continued east, moving back over Lake Hartwell, where some trees were blown down on islands. The tornado apparently dissipated over the lake. East of Snyder Rd, damage was almost exclusively confined to snapped and uprooted trees, although some boat shelters and docks on Lake Hartwell were lifted and tossed as much as 100 feet. This tornado was produced by a supercell thunderstorm.
Public reported an area of significant wind damage, with numerous trees snapped off and uprooted along Faris Rd near Greenville Memorial Hospital, extending east to Sunset Dr and Augusta St.
Portion of the roof removed from a public building on McGee Rd.
Numerous trees were blown down around the city of Anderson.

This tornado began along Old Williamston Rd near its intersection with Brooks Rd. The tornado traveled northeast, paralleling Old Williamston Rd before crossing Boggs Rd and Opp Rd, then lifting near the intersection of Brown Rd and highway 29. Damage was confined to uprooted trees along the path, with a few smaller trees snapped off. The tornado was produced by a supercell thunderstorm as it was being overtaken by a line of storms.
Quite a few trees were blown down from the town of Dewy Rose to Ruckersville Rd.
Several trees were blown down along highway 28, with at least one tree on a home.
Numerous trees were blown down along Old Calhoun Falls Rd. Part of the roof of a home was also severely damaged, and some siding was torn off. A tree fell through the roof of another home.

NWS survey found an extensive area of damage in the city of Abbeville consistent with a strong EF2 tornado. The tornado began near the intersection of highway 71 and Rock Hill Rd before moving east/southeast through the city of Abbeville. The main areas affected in the city were Church Street, McGowan, Ave, Main St, and especially Secession Ave. The roofs were blown off about a half dozen frame homes in the city, while numerous mobile homes were heavily damaged or destroyed. A few other office buildings and businesses received major roof damage in this area. Numerous trees were snapped off or uprooted along the path. One tree fell through a home, injuring the man inside. Another man caught outside received head injuries from flying debris. The tornado lifted about a mile east/southeast of the city. The tornado was produced by a supercell embedded in a line of rapidly moving storms.

NWS survey found an area of tornado damage that began about 3 miles southwest of Jonesville in the Proctor/Zig Zag Rd area. Several trees were snapped off or uprooted in this area and some outdoor objects blown around. The tornado moved almost due east to T Bishop Rd, where a mobile home was destroyed and another heavily damaged. Dozens of trees were also uprooted and snapped off in this area. The tornado continued along an intermittent path to the east before uprooting numerous pine and cedar trees on Jonesville Highway about 3 miles southeast of Jonesville. A 3-ton trailer was moved about 100 feet, and a home received minor roof damage at this location. The tornado continued on to Bob Little Rd, where a plant building received major roof damage. The tornado then damaged two mobile homes before lifting 3.5 SE of Jonesville.
Trees were blown down across the town of Laurens.

NWS survey identified a tornado path that began near the intersection of Hunters Creek Bvd and Woodlawn Rd. The tornado continued east/southeast across the south side of Greenwood, uprooting or snapping off numerous trees along the path. The hardest hit area was around Edgefield St, where numerous trees were damaged. Some trees fell on and seriously damaged homes. Other homes received significant roof damage.

A second tornado path was found a couple of miles north of the main tornado track through Greenwood. This tornado began on Karlie Ct just off Laurel Rd. Once again, numerous trees were uprooted or snapped off. However, more structural damage was observed along this path. Several homes received minor to moderate roof damage. Siding and gutters were blown off a few homes as well. A home near the end of the path received the most significant, damage, with part of the roof completely blown off and and the collapse of an adjacent exterior wall. A storage trailer was also blown over in this area. Also, a tree fell across a train track on Emerald Rd, causing a train to derail.
At least two trees were blown down across roads in the northwest corner of the county.
Hail reported in the Epworth community.
A large section was torn off of a metal building at a paper plant. Several trees were also blown down in the area.
A large barn was destroyed, and several houses had shingles removed by the wind. The brick veneer was torn off a church and trees were blown onto homes.
Siding was torn off a home and large limbs were blown down in Great Falls. Trees were blown down 2 miles south of Ft Lawn.
Trees were blown down on Whetstone Rd and Lex Road.
Trees were down on Biggerstaff Rd and Fairview Church Rd.
A tree was blown down in Six Mile and another in Central around the same time.
Hail was reported on Jennings Rd.
Hail was reported on highway 25.
Lightning struck a storage shed on S Depot St, igniting a fire that destroyed the building and its contents.

Flash flooding developed across the southern and eastern sides of the city after thunderstorms dumped 3 to 5 inches of rain across the area in a couple of hours. Although much of the flooding was due to poor drainage, Briar Creek, Little Sugar Creek, and other small streams flooded. Numerous motorists were trapped and required rescuing due to flood water, with the most serious situations occurring on Independence Bvd near Wendover Rd, Wellesley Ave near Freedom Park, and on East Bvd at Maryland Ave. Some residents had to be evacuated from an apartment complex on Monroe Rd due to flooding along Briar Creek.
Although heavy rainfall ended across the Charlotte area around 7 pm, flood water continued to affect the area before receding during the late evening.

Water entered a church on highway 23 due to flooding along Little Creek. Water flowed into several additional yards along the creek. Broadcast media reported residents said the water level was the highest it had been in at least 15 years. A few rock and mud slides were also reported in the area.
Cane Creek flooded a bridge on Mills Gap Rd. Also, a swelling creek eroded a bank in a development just west of Fletcher, causing sediment to enter several homes.

Flood waters entered a home along Row Branch. Birchfield Creek also flooded Birchfield Creek Rd. Flooding along Roaring Creek caused highway 19E to become impassable for a while, and some private bridges were washed out along Roaring Creek.
Flooding along Kings Creek and Blue Creek sent water over portions of Blue Creek Rd, Grandin Rd, and highway 18. Mud slides were also reported in the area.

Flooding along Cranberry Creek covered portions of highway 19 from a mile east of Elk Park to the Cranberry community, causing the road to be closed for a while. Water from the creek also entered some homes.

Flooding along Allen Branch caused water to damage the underpinnings of some mobile homes along Tequila Heights (1 NE). Also, water from Cope Creek entered some apartment buildings and a business on Bridge St.
Queens Creek flooded highway 18 near St Johns Church Ave.

Several small streams came out of their banks in the Love Valley area, including Snow Creek, Dishmon Creek, and Little Rocky Creek. Flooding of numerous intersections was reported due to poor drainage, including at Tyvola Rd and I-77, where two vehicles were reported floating through high water.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding along Brier Creek, covering portions of Brier Creek Rd. Several residents were trapped by the rising water.
Trees and power lines were blown down on the west and north side of the city of Pickens.
A tree was blown onto power lines in the Liberty area.
Multiple trees were blown down just off highway 123 near the South Carolina state line.
A spotter reported penny size hail and measured a wind gust of 56 MPH.
Lightning struck a home on Summit Ridge Ln, causing extensive damage.
Lightning ignited a fire at a home on Wilson Rd, about two miles east northeast of Brevard, causing damage to the roof and attic.
Lightning struck a large home on Pimlico Ln, igniting a fire that caused enough damage to render the home uninhabitable.
Numerous trees were blown down across the western half of the county.
A tree and a power pole were blown down on the north side of Lake Burton.
A few trees were blown down in Chau Ram State Park. This is just off highway 76 about 3 miles west northwest of Westminster.
Hail up to the size of quarters fell over the northern part of the town of Drexel, including along Williams Rd.
Golf ball size hail was reported on Bethany Church Rd on the southwest side of Forest City.
This storm produced quite a bit of hail over the north central part of the county, including near the intersection of highways 208 and 12 where hail was reported to be 3 inches deep.
Hail was reported on Patton Ave on the southwest side of Asheville.
The large hail caused significant damage to apple crops in this part of Henderson County.
Hail up to size of quarters fell near Edneyville.
Penny to nickel size hail was reported near the intersection of highway 74 and I-26 on the west side of the town of Columbus.
Several trees were blown down in and around the city of Marion.
Four to five inch diameter tree limbs were blown down between Tigerville and highway 11.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Inman Mills.
A few trees and power lines were blown down over the northwest side of the County. A tree fell on a shed in the Inman Mills community.

Clear Creek overflowed its banks, flooding a portion of Fruitland Rd. A motorist had to be rescued on Fruitland Rd after driving through high water. Stream flooding was also reported on Dana Rd and Howard Gap Rd. Also, county comms reported flooding of Willow Rd due to an overflowing stream.

Wilson Rd was closed due to flooding along the French Broad River. Davidson River Rd was also closed when the Davidson River overflowed its banks. In addition, Green Rd and Barclay Rd were covered with water from overflowing streams.
Creeks flooded several roads in the northern part of the county, including Cassidy Bridge Rd and Whetstone Rd. Several roads were also flooded in Walhalla, including Andover Dr.

Although rain rates diminished during mid-morning, flooding persisted in the Green River Cove Rd area through the remainder of the morning, with evacuations becoming necessary. In addition to the flooding, saturated soil resulted in quite a few fallen trees and isolated small landslides.

Although flash flooding ended across the area around sunrise, persistent moderate to heavy rainfall caused high water conditions to persist in central Henderson County through the morning hours. Flooding also expanded to areas near Mills River, as Butler Bridge Rd was closed about 8 miles northwest of Hendersonville. In addition to the flooding, saturated soil resulted in quite a few fallen trees and isolated small landslides.

Severe flash flooding affected Stephens County. Numerous creeks left their banks in the central and western part of the county, including Toccoa Creek which flooded highway 17. Portions of highway 441 and 123 were also closed. At least 300 homes in the county suffered flood damage. Uninsured property losses were estimated to be over 2 million dollars, and damage to roads and water lines was estimated to be around 3 million. A 20 foot section of Dick's Hill Parkway, the major road between Toccoa and Cornelia, was washed away.

Water from a stream flowed over Rodeo Circle. Several other roads were flooded with several feet of water off highway 17 near Clarkesville. Additionally, a stream gauge on the Soque River at highway 197 went above its established flood stage.
Flash flooding developed along the Green River, forcing evacuations and closing Green River Cove Rd. Water reportedly entered several homes along the River, with water up to the windows of one home.

The very heavy rainfall that caused flash flooding early in the day ended by early  afternoon. However, periods of moderate to heavy rain caused flooding to persist in areas from Long Creek to Walhalla through the afternoon. At the height of the event, 33 roads were closed in this area. In addition to the flooding, quite a few trees fell in the saturated soil.

Although flash flooding ended across the area around sunrise, persistent moderate to heavy rainfall caused high water conditions to persist in the French Broad valley through the morning hours. In addition to the flooding, several small mudslides occurred and quite a few trees fell in the saturated soil.

The very heavy rainfall that caused flash flooding early in the day ended by early afternoon. However, periods of moderate to heavy rain caused flooding to persist across the Toccoa area through the afternoon. New flooding also developed along the Broad River. Large sections of Yearwood St and highway 123 to the southwest of Toccoa were washed out during this time. The heavy rain also washed out some water lines, causing 5000 customers to lose water service. A sewage spill also occurred.17.63 inches of rain was reported in Toccoa for the period from the 18th-22nd.

An extended period of moderate to heavy rain resulted in flooding along the Mills River. Portions of South Mills River Rd and River Loop Rd were covered in water. Also, flooding began on the French Broad River near Etowah around this time, covering portions of highway 64, Pleasant Grove Rd, and Willow Rd with water. A total of 35 roads in Henderson and Transylvania Counties were blocked by flood waters. River flooding continued until the evening hours on the 24th.

Flooding developed near the headwaters of the French Broad River which covered Main St in Rosman with about a foot of water. Water also entered an apartment building. Also, the Davidson River flooded near Brevard, flooding a portion of Davidson River Rd and Wilson Rd. Turkey Creek flooded Deavor Rd in Pisgah Forest. A total of 35 roads in Henderson and Transylvania Counties were blocked by flood water.

Settlement Rd was flooded in Webster and Dillard Rd was closed due to flooding in Sylva. Also, Roy Tritt Rd was reported to be under water and closed two miles southeast of Cullowhee as was Helen Zachary Rd.

Flooding developed in several spots along the Little Tennessee River after an extended period of heavy rainfall. Several roads were closed, including Arthur Drake Rd and Riverside Rd. At least one motorist required rescue after driving over a flooded road. Water entered and damaged several homes along the river. In addition, water from Cartoogechaye Creek surrounded several homes on Patton Creekside Dr.
Several trees were down near the intersection of Rocky Ford Rd and Powell Bridge Rd.
Trees were blown down on Liberty Church Road, a little more than 6 miles west of Farmington.
Large tree limbs were blown down three miles northeast of Farmington.
A severe storm produced several instances of hail, including at I-85 near mile marker 67, Spartanburg Methodist College and in the city.
Two trees were blown down.
A small creek overflowed its banks, flooding Henrietta St and Poplar St in Toccoa.
Lightning ignited a fire that caused damage at a home on Doolie Rd.

Flooding developed briefly along a portion of the Cullasaja River during the morning. River Rd was covered by water for a short time. Also, two wastewater spills occurred closer to town due to the heavy rain.

After 3 to 4 inches of rain fell over a widespread area in about a twelve-hour period, flooding developed along Wahachee Creek, affecting portions of Edison Rd and Dr. George Ward Rd. Both roads were closed. Also, Beaverdam Creek overflowed its banks in the northern part of the county, flooding Horse Farm Rd and Brickyard Rd and flooding a restaurant on Brewers Bridge Rd. Kurt Anderson Rd was also closed for a while.

Several streams flooded across Henderson County, and severe urban flooding developed in the Hendersonville area. Mud Creek flooded portions of highway 25 and highway 176. Roads that were closed in the county included Dana Rd, Fruitland Rd and Tracy Grove Rd in Hendersonville.
Irwin Ave was closed at South Church St due to flooding along Beaverdam Creek.
Old River Road was closed due to flooding along the Tuckaseegee River about a mile east of Bryson City. Also, Needmore Rd was closed due to flooding of the Little Tennessee River.
A stream gauge reported that Back Creek briefly went above flood stage in the southwest part of the county. Rocky River Rd was closed near Pharr Mill Rd due to flooding along the Rocky River.
Mount Lebanon Rd was closed due to flooding along the Middle Tyger River.

Although heavy rain began to taper off during the morning, flooding persisted along a few smaller streams into the late morning in response to 4 to 6 inches of storm total rainfall. In addition, minor flooding developed briefly in spots along the French Broad River.
Although heavy rain began to taper off after sunrise, flooding continued along portions of the Tyger River through late morning in response to runoff from 4 to 5 inches of storm total rainfall.
Flooding continued along portions of Back Creek and the Rocky Broad River into the evening hours. Total rainfall amounts of 4-5 inches occurred, mostly within a 24-hour period.
Although heavy rain began to taper off during the pre-dawn hours, flooding persisted into the early afternoon in response to runoff from 3 to 4 inches of storm total rainfall.

Several roads were closed in the Brevard area, apparently due to flooding along creeks and streams that backed up due to a combination of heavy rain and flooding along the French Broad River. Closed roads included Green Rd to the southwest of Brevard, and Cascade Lake Rd  and Wilson Rd on the southeast side of town.
Flooding developed along lower portions of the Reedy River in response to runoff from 4 to 5 inches of storm total rainfall.
Very windy conditions downed several trees and power lines. A few trees fell on homes, with at least one home in the Newton area sustaining damage.
Very windy conditions downed several trees and power lines. A few trees fell on homes, with at least one home one the southeast side of Charlotte sustaining damage.
Very windy conditions downed several trees across the county. One person was killed when a tree fell on him as he was getting out of his car.
A motorist was killed about 6 miles southeast of Anderson when he collided with a tree that had previously fallen.
Water entered the basement of a home on North Main St, apparently due to flooding caused by poor drainage after 3 to 5 inches of rain fell over an extended period.

Flash flooding developed in and around the city of Anderson, with several roads closed due to high water. Although most of the flooding was of the urban/poor drainage variety, at least two creeks were involved, including Whitner and Cox Creeks. Affected roads included Southwood St (due to Whitner Creek) and Rantowles Rd (due to Cox Creek), where water entered some homes. At least a half dozen additional streets were closed in the city due to urban flooding. These included Susan St and Booker St, which were covered by as much as 3 feet of water.

Quite a few roads closed due to flooding throughout the Greenville and Greer areas. Although most of the flooding was due to poor drainage, some streams were involved, particularly the Reedy River. Some of the roads affected included Hudson Rd, which was closed at Prestige Ct.  A portion of Brushy Creek Rd was closed, as well as Boiling Springs Rd near Sugar Creek Rd, where over a foot of water covered about a 200-foot section of the road. Also, portions of Hammett Bridge Rd were closed. The Reedy River exceeded established flood stage in downtown Greenville, flooding portions of Cleveland Park.

Roads closed due to flooding included Shiloh Church Rd about 7 miles south of Hartwell, Page Rd about 3.5 miles southeast of town, and Heritage Rd on the south side of Lake Hartwell. Some flooding was the result of streams, some due to poor drainage.
A bridge was washed out on Kurt Anderson Rd.

Official NWS stream gauges indicated several streams rose to levels well above established flood stages, including Mud Creek on the south side of Hendersonville, Bat Fork Creek on the east side and Clear Creek about 5 miles northeast of the city. Affected roads included Airport Rd, King St, Grove St, and Fruitland Rd.
McMullen Creek exceeded its established flood stage and flooded portions of Addison Dr and Willhaven Rd.

Flooding developed at several locations in the southeast part of the county after heavy rain fell throughout the morning. The main problem area was along Wildcat Creek, where a stream gauge exceeded the established flood stage by 2 feet, forcing the closure of McConnells Highway. Gunsmoke Rd was also closed at Hawley Rd, about 12 miles west southwest of Rock Hill. This was due to flooding along Conrad Creek. Saluda Rd was also closed at highway 324, likely due to flooding along Stony Fork.

Although heavy rain began to wind down across the area during the late afternoon and early evening, flooding persisted in some areas, while new flooding developed, as runoff worked its way through the waterways. Floodwaters gradually moved down the Reedy River to the Simpsonville area, where flooding did not subside until 6 AM on the 3rd.

After 3-4 inches of rain fell over a 12-24 hour period, a stream gauage on the Middle Tyger River went above the established flood stage at the site. Several roads were flooded downstream in the Lake Lyman area.

After 3-4 inches of rain fell over a 12-24 hour period, a stream gauage on the Middle Tyger River went above the established flood stage at the site, flooding the approaches to the bridge on Mount Labanon Rd.
Several trailers were flooded along the Oconoluftee River just off highway 441 in Cherokee.
The stream gauge on the Tuckasegee River at Bryson City briefly went above the established flood stage.
Urban and poor drainage flooding caused closure of a handful of roads in the northern half of Spartanburg County, including Campbell Ave in Landrum.
Urban and poor drainage flooding caused closure of a handful of roads in the northern half of Spartanburg County, including portions of Monks Grove Church Rd and highway 221 near Spartanburg.
Trees were blown down along highway 79 about 12 miles east southeast of Elberton.
Several trees were blown down near the intersection of highways 254, 246 and 25, about 8 miles west northwest of the city of Greenwood.
Several trees were blown down in and around the city of Abbeville.

A small, but intense downburst affected the north side of the Cross Hill community. Damage began near the intersection of highways 72 and 39 and extended to the Puckett Ferry Rd and Liberty Springs Rd area. An unanchored mobile home was flipped and several other mobile homes were damaged. A shed was also flipped onto a carport. Numerous trees were also downed in the area.

A downburst damage pattern began near the intersection of highway 25 and Keels Rd, about 5 miles northwest of Greenwood. Tree damage was sporadic in this area, before becoming more widespread in locations around Highland Dr and Rutledge Rd. A tree fell on a carport and some shingles were blown off a home on North Lake Dr. Finally, a large tree fell on and significantly damaged an animal hospital on highway 72 on the northeast side of town.
A couple trees were blown down along Center St on the northwest side of Greenwood.
Urban and poor drainage flooding of highway 70 near Hildebran and Main St in Glen Alpine was reported.
Saluda Rd was closed at the intersection of Foote St due to urban flooding.
West Oak St was closed between Pennington Rd and Mt Gallant Rd due to flooding.
Flooding developed along Mud Creek, Bat Creek, and Clear Creek. Roads flooded by these streams include New Hope Rd, Dana Rd, Tracy Grove Rd, Airport Rd, Grove St, King St, and Fruitland Rd.

Several areas of stream flooding developed across the southern half of the county. Roads closed by flood waters included Broad River Rd, North Ave and Avalon Rd, all of which were on the southast side of the county.

Widespread flooding developed over the southern and central part of the county, with most of the flooding concentrated in areas from Walhalla to Fair Play. Numerous roads were closed, some due to poor drainage, others due to flooded streams.
Mount Olive Church Rd was closed due to high water conditions about 6 miles north northwest of Taylorsville.
Highway 16 South was closed due to high water conditions to the south of Taylorsville.

Overflowing streams caused widespread flooding across Catawba County. Closed roads included the intersection of Sain Rd and Pittstown Rd due to flooding along Hop Creek. South D Ave was closed in Maiden. In the Newton area, Little Mountain Rd was closed, as was East Bandys Cross Rd. Rocky Ford Rd was closed at the bridge were it crosses the South Fork Catawba River.

Widespread flooding developed across the county, with numerous roads closed, some due to poor drainage, and some due to overflowing streams. This included a bridge that was washed out on Massapoag Rd a little south of Lincolnton.

The Little River exceeded its established flood stage, flooding the intersection of Merrill Rd and Cascade Lake Rd. Other roads that were closed due to flooding were Hannah Ford Rd about 5 miles southwest of Brevard, Wilson Rd on the east side of town and Davidson River Rd about 3 miles northeast of Brevard.

A combination of poor drainage and stream flooding, mainly over the northwest corner of Spartanburg County, closed several roads.  The main stream involved in this flooding was the Middle Tyger and some of its smaller feeder streams. Closed roads included Highway 14 near Oak Grove Rd and where it crosses the Pacolet River, Mount Lebanon Church Rd, Old Mill Rd and Waspnest Rd.

Mainly urban flooding, along with some stream flooding, developed across central Greenville County. The Reedy River exceeded its established flood stage in downtown Greenville by 2 feet. Closed roads included Boiling Springs Rd at Sugar Creek Rd, Garlington Rd at I-385 and Poplar St.

A combination of urban and stream flooding closed roads in and around the Anderson metro area. Affected roads included Welpine Dr near Marrett Rd just to the north of Interstate 85. In Anderson, urban flooding briefly closed McGee Rd, highway 29, W Hampton St, and W Reed St.
The bridge on Blake Dairy Rd, three miles east of Belton was closed due to high water.

Numerous roads were flooded, mainly across the eastern half of the county. This included highway 274, 10 miles north northwest of Rock Hill, which was impassable. A small creek overflowed its banks, flooding several townhomes located on highway 21 in the Fort Mill area. Severe urban flooding developed on the east side of Rock Hill, with 5 motorists requiring rescue from their automobiles at Red Rock Rd and Dave Lyle Bvd. Additionally, several stream gauges exceeded established flood stage across the|eastern half of the county, including Wildcat Creek and Big Dutchman Creek. Roads affected by these flooding streams include Mount Gallant Rd, West Oak Rd, McConnels Highway, and Ogden Rd.
Little Dove Creek overflowed the bridge on Hobbs Noggle Rd.
Bullards Ferry Rd and Addison Rd were closed due to flooding.

Significant flooding developed along Back Creek in the city of Harrisburg. Several roads were closed by flood waters, including Caldwell Rd, Stallings Rd, and Pharr Mill Rd. One swift water rescue was required, and water entered homes on Blackjack Oak Ct, where Fuda Creek runs into Back Creek.

Several roads were closed due to flooding streams on the west side of the county. Affected roads included highway 126 at Brookstone Rd, Browning Rd at|Pea Ridge Rd, Conley Rd at Jeeter Carswell Rd and Conley at Bryd Rd. Also, a mobile home park was evacuated on Antioch Rd, about 5 miles northeast of Morganton, due to a flooding stream.
Old River Rd was flooded and closed through Bryson City.

Urban and small stream flooding developed throughout the city of Salisbury and surrounding areas. Although most flooding was due to poor drainage, Grants Creek and Town Creek overflowed their banks near the city. Closed roads included Innes St at I-85, Jake Alexander Bvd, Sunset Dr, and Happy Lake Rd about 8 miles south of Salisbury. A woman was rescued from her car on Old Concord Rd, which was flooded by Dutch Buffalo Creek 9 miles south southwest of town. Also, urban flooding developed on the Rowan side of Kannapolis, with Crestmont St closed and water entering an apartment building.

A combination of urban flooding and small stream flooding developed across much of the southern and eastern half of Mecklenburg County. The Briar Creek basin was hardest hit, with numerous roads closed along the creek and several rescues required|from vehicles. A few of the closed roads included Independence Bvd, Shannonhouse Dr, Dunlavin Way, and Country Club Dr. Other closed roads included Reedy Creek Rd 11 miles east of town, Sharon Rd, Lancaster Highway 13 miles south of town, Woodland Dr at Commonwealth Ave, and Eastway Dr.

Widespread flooding was reported across the county, with numerous roads closed, some due to poor drainage, some due to overflowing streams. A few of the affected roads included Dash Rd and Saw Mill Rd, about 18 miles north northeast of Statesville, Shady Rest Rd and Amble Rd.

Significant urban flooding developed on the Cabarrus side of Kannapolis, with numerous roads closed due to high water. Affected roads included Verona, Fairview, Eddleman, South Little Texas, Pine, and Trinity Church Rd. Evacuations became necessary on Pine St and Verona St.

Significant urban flooding developed on the Cabarrus side of Kannapolis, with numerous roads closed due to high water. Affected roads included Verona, Fairview, Eddleman, South Little Texas, Pine, and Trinity Church Rd. Evacuations became necessary on Pine St and Verona St.
Although heavy rainfall ended across the county around midnight, high water conditions persisted across northern sections of the county through the rest of the night.

Although heavy rainfall ended across the area shortly after midnight, runoff from the  earlier rain caused high water conditions to persist across much of the western half of the county through the overnight hours. Also, flooding developed along the Johns River during this time. Most of the flooding ended by 6 am, though a few larger streams remained in flood into the afternoon hours.

Although heavy rain ended across the area around midnight, runoff from the earlier rainfall caused flooding to persist across portions of Greenville County through the rest of the night. Flooding along the Reedy River persisted into the afternoon hours.
Although heavy rain ended across the area by midnight, runoff from earlier rainfall caused high water conditions to persist across the county through the rest of the night.
Although heavy rainfall ended over the county shortly after midnight, runoff resulted in|persistent high water conditions through much of the rest of the night.
Although heavy rainfall ended across the area during the early morning hours, high water conditions persisted until after sunrise across the Charlotte metro area.

Although heavy rain ended across the county shortly after midnight, runoff from the earlier rainfall caused flooding to persist across the eastern half of the county until after sunrise.
Numerous trees were blown down between Westminster and Fair Play.
A combination of gusty winds and saturated soil from heavy rainfall caused a tree to fall on an automobile on Sedgewood Dr.
Poor drainage resulted in water entering a building in downtown Columbus after 3 to 4 inches of rain fell in about an 18-hour period.

A combination of gusty winds and saturated ground from the previous night���s heavy rainfall caused a tree to fell on Lower Dallas Highway, crushing an automobile and killing the 72-year-old woman who was driving.

Although heavy rain ended across the area shortly after midnight, runoff from the earlier rainfall caused flooding to persist, while some new flooding developed on larger streams. This included Hunting Creek in the northern part of the county.

Although heavy rain ended across the county by midnight, runoff from the day's heavy rainfall resulted in a continuation of high water, while new flooding developed along the French Broad River in the eastern portion of the county during this time. River flooding persisted until late on the 27th. Major flooding was observed briefly at the Blantyre river gauge.
Flooding developed along the Reedy River in the Simpsonville area in the late afternoon, flooding Marler Rd.
The Reedy River exceeded established flood stage in downtown Greenville during the early afternoon, flooding portions of Cleveland Park.
Flooding developed in the northern part of the county along portions of the Middle|Tyger, with Mount Lebanon Rd under water for a while.
A stream gauge on the South Pacolet River exceeded established flood stage during mid-afternoon, indicating that a portion of highway 14 was flooded in the Landrum area.
A stream gauge along Goose Creek indicated the stream briefly exceeded established flood stage, flooding a few roads in locations near the junction of highway 218 and highway 601.
A gauge on The Rocky River exceeded established flood stage above Irish Buffalo|Creek, indicating flooding of Pharr Mill Rd and Mount Pleasant Rd.

A stream gauge on Wildcat Creek exceeded the established flood stage, indicating flooding of McConnells Highway, as well as portions of Saluda Rd and highway 324. Also, Gunsmoke Rd was closed due to a flooding stream.
A stream overflowed its banks in the city, flooding the intersection of Hill Crest Dr and Whitmire Rd.
The French Broad River exceeded flood stage at Blantyre early on the 6th, and remained in flood until the afternoon of the 7th.
River flooding developed along the South Fork Catawba River near Lowell during the afternoon of the 5th and persisted through the early part of the 7th.
A tree was blown down on Riverfork Rd and another on Cannon Rd about 4 miles west southwest of Waterloo.
Several reports of hail ranging in size from dimes to golf balls were received from the Mooresville area.

A very short tornado path was surveyed near Belmont. The tornado touched down in the Parkdale Dr/Landing Rd area, where a mill was damaged. Part of the metal sheet roofing was peeled back and thrown in multiple directions, allowing some interior walls to collapse. A tractor trailer was also overturned on the south side of the mill. Several homes were damaged at a mobile home park adjacent to the mill, where a number of trees were also blown down. The tornado traveled roughly 200 yards before lifting.

Area of straight line wind damage was surveyed, which extended from Sam Wilson Rd north to Mount Holly Rd in western Mecklenburg County. Numerous trees were blown down, with one tree falling on and causing significant damage to a home.
Multiple large limbs were blown down across the city.
Golf ball size hail was reported by a spotter near the Greenville/Pickens Speedway.

A line of severe thunderstorms produced a swath of large hail between the towns of Welcome and Travelers Rest in the western part of the county, eastward to the Spartanburg County line around Greer. Numerous reports of hail to the size of golf balls were received. The area of large hail was about 10 miles wide in the western part of the county and narrowed down to about 5 miles in the east. No dollar  estimates were available, but there was considerable damage to cars and roofs.
Multiple tree limbs were blown down west of Gowensville.
Hail slightly larger than quarter size was reported near the intersection of highways 296 and 290.
Hail was reported a little to the north of the town of Moore.
Half dollar size hail was reported just to the west of Westgate Mall.

Large trees were blown down on Cannons Campground Road, between 5 and 6 miles northeast of Spartanburg.
A large tree and several large limbs were blown down between Mooresboro and Boiling Springs.
There were a couple reports of half dollar size hail from the south side of Simpsonville.

A number of spotters and county officials reported quarter to golf ball size hail in areas from just east of Cowpens to downtown Gaffney to the Edgewater and highway 18 intersection to mile marker 96 on I-85.
Several trees were blown down a little ways east of the Spartanburg county line.
Trees were blown down about 3 miles southeast of Blacksburg.
A tree fell on and detroyed a mobile home on Lurecliff Dr.
Two trees were snapped off by strong winds on Battleground Rd a little north of the South Carolina state line.
Golf ball size hail was reported on Old Landfill Rd, about 7.5 miles northwest of Abbeville.
Some vehicles were damaged by large hail in this area.
Two large trees were blown down on Steeplechase Dr about 4 miles southeast of Gastonia.
A few trees were blown down about 6 miles north northeast of Gray Court.
Hail, up to the size of quarters, covered the ground at the Jonesville Fire Department.

Quarter size hail was reported at the intersection of I-77 and I-485.
Several trees were blown down in this area.
Lightning struck a power line on Fawn Hill Rd, which resulted in minor injuries to two people in two different homes. Small fires ignited in both homes, causing some minor damage.
Lightning ignited a fire at an apartment building on Riverstone Ct, causing damage to the roof.

This tornado touched down along highway 29 in Spencer, just east of the town center, where the facade and roof of a shopping center were damaged. The tornado traveled northeast along Salisbury Ave, causing mainly minor roof damage to numerous homes, and blowing the awning off a business. The brick chimney was blown off a home and two trees fell on another home in this area. The tornado continued northeast to the Yadkin Ave/Cain St area, where numerous trees were blown down, one on a home, another on an apartment building, and one on an automobile. Numerous homes received minor roof damage as the tornado continued northeast, eventually crossing N Salisbury Ave again. The most significant damage occurred in the Hackett St area, where a shed and boat awning were destroyed. A large tree also fell on a house in this area, causing significant damage. The tornado then caused minor damage at a factory before took on more of a east/northeast heading, roughly paralleling Hackett St, where additional tree damage occurred. The tornado continued east/northeast, crossing I-85 just north of Hackett St before crossing the Yadkin River into Davidson County.
Trees and power lines were blown down about 3 miles southeast of Vale.
Trees were blown down in a roadway about 3 miles southeast of Statesville.
Trees were blown down near mile marker 26 on Interstate 85.
Trees were blown down along highway 187 near Lake Hartwell.
Power lines were blown down along highway 25 near the Donaldson Center. A couple trees were blown down in the area as well.
Trees were blown down near I-85 north of Anderson.

Straight line winds affected an area between Lawndale and Belwood. Several trees were uprooted, one of which fell on a manufactured home on West Stagecoach Trail just west of Lawndale. In addition, half the roof was blown off a barn on Old Belwood Rd.

A short tornado track was surveyed in the Fair Play community. The tornado touched down along highway 59 between Cleveland Creek Rd and Doctors Rd. Part of the roof was blown off a manufactured home at this location, and numerous trees were snapped off or uprooted. The tornado continued in a northeast direction toward the Pine Grove Rd area, where damage to trees continued near the intersection of Grant Rd. The tornado appeared to dissipate in this area.

A tornado damage path began in the Harper Rd area of Pendleton. A large detached garage had its windward-facing doors blown in. This caused a large cargo door on the back side of the garage to blow out. Several horse stables on Harper Rd had metal roofs partially peeled back or blown off. Numerous trees were snapped off in this area, with a few large trees uprooted. The tornado continued northeast to Liberty Highway, just south of the Cherry St extension. The metal roofing was partially torn off a barn at this location, and several outbuildings were damaged or blown away. A large, well-constructed home received minor eaves damage. The tornado turned in a more east northeasterly direction at this point, dissipating shortly after crossing Liberty Highway.

Lightning struck and injured a woman on Fieldstone Dr in Mooresville. Another woman was struck at another location in Mooresville at around the same time.
Gusty winds from a thunderstorm caused choppy waters to develop on Lake Norman, resulting in the drowning of a 17-year-old and an 11-year-old boy.
Lightning struck a house on Tiffany St, igniting a fire that damaged part of the structure.
Lightning ignited a fire at a home on Poplar Leaf Dr, destroying the home.
Lightning ignited a fire that destroyed a home on Sunny Brae Dr.
Lightning struck a home on Player Circle, igniting a fire that resulted in some minor roof damage.
Lightning ignited a fire at a home on Langhorne Ave, causing significant damage.
Lightning ignited a fire at a home on Tripper Ln, causing significant damage.

Several roads were flooded throughout the city due to poor drainage. A gage along McMullen Creek went about a foot above flood stage at Addison Dr and Lincrest Place, about 5 miles southeast of Uptown, and flooding along Briar Creek was reported in the South Park area.

Highway 25 was flooded by Cuffytown Creek, and Bowie Rd and Bethel Rd were flooded by Beaverdam Creek after as much as 6 inches of rain fell over a few hours time across the extreme southern part of the county.
Several trees were blown down along highway 212, about 13 miles north of Marshall.
A tree was blown down on Bartlett Hollow Rd and another was blown down in the same area on Bat Cave Rd.
Several large tree limbs were blown down at Caesars Head State Park.
Quarter size hail fell at the River Creek Campground.
Multiple trees were blown down on Adams Hill Rd, on the northwest side of Asheville. Some trees fell on vehicles.
Several trees and large limbs were blown down in and around the city of Patterson.
A couple trees were blown down on highway 80, several miles northwest of Marion.
Several large trees were blown down on Paul Payne Store Rd. A chimney was also blown off the roof of a home near this location.
Power lines were blown down on Temple Hill Church Rd, a little over 7 miles southeast of Lenoir. A tree was blown down in the same area.
Large tree limbs were blown down on Brown Mountain Beach Rd in the extreme western part of the county.
Power lines were blown down about 3 miles northeast of Hickory.
Power lines were blown down on Cloninger St in Claremont.
Two large trees were blown down on Shiloh Rd.
A tree was blown down on Big Laurel Rd.
