Two trees fell onto an apartment complex due to saturated soil.

Parts of Upper Shut-In road were further damaged by high stream levels after very heavy rain. An earlier flood had significantly under-cut parts of the road. Water was also reported over parts of River Road in this same area. Several small landslides also affected River Road and Upper Shut-In road in this same area.
A few trees were blown down near Fairview.
Trees were blown down on Collinsville Rd and John Weaver Rd in the Green Creek community.
Several trees were blown down along Oak Hill School Rd. One tree fell on and caused minor damage to the school's structure. Other trees fell on a home and a large utility building.
A few trees were blown down along highway 29 west of Spartanburg.
Penny size hail fell along Carmichael Court.
Multiple trees were blown down in the Boiling Springs area. A tree was also blown down a little west of town, at Spring Valley Rd and Clark Rd.
Water was around two feet deep in parts of the Carlyle Point Subdivision, near the intersection Boiling Springs Rd. Water was about half way up the wheels of a few cars.
Two trees were blown down in the Callison community.
Deep ponding of water was impeding traffic at the intersection of I-85 and Laurens Road.
Multiple trees were blown down in the Bad Creek area.
Four roads in the Drexel area were flooded and closed.

Little Gunpowder Creek flooded a park to a depth of at least a foot. Broadcast Media video showed Zacks Fork Creek flooding Powell Road. Pennell Rd NE was also flooded by a stream in this area along the Lenoir Greenway. Cottrell Hill Road was flooded and closed in front of Chapel of Hope Church, near the intersection of Severt Circle (3 NE Lenoir).
Local fire department encountered flooding on Oak Hill Road while responding to a call.
Trees were blown down at the intersection of highways 276 and 414 and on Mountain View Rd near Tigerville.
Trees were blown down on State Park Rd at Jennfier Ct, extending east to the Taylors area.
Trees were blown down on Amity Rd, about 4 miles east of Anderson.

Trees were blown down on Belton-Honea Path Highway, 2 miles northwest of Honea Path, and at the intersection of highways 178 and 76 in Honea Path. Other trees|were blown down on Firetower Rd and Austin Rd, both about 4 miles west Honea Path.

An NWS Storm Survey found an area of sporadic straight line wind damage several hundred yards south of a tornado path. Occasional downed trees were found along Emily Lane, then continuing beyond the tornado track across Augusta Rd, Reedy Fork Rd, and Fork Shoals Rd.
A funnel cloud was reported near Simpsonville by a storm chaser.
Multiple trees were blown down in the Lake Wylie area.
Multiple trees and power lines were blown down across the city. Power lines fell on a vehicle on Park Dr (3 S) and a tree fell on a vehicle on Seneca Place.
Multiple trees, large limbs, and power lines were blown down across Concord, with several roads blocked.
Multiple trees were blown down on Flowering Tree Lane about 4 miles southwest of Rockwell.

NWS survey team found the path of a weak tornado that began in a wooded area just northeast of Lauren Trace Circle. A few trees were downed at this location, with one tree taking down a power line. The tornado intensified as it moved east/northeast from there, downing multiple trees and snapping numerous large limbs along a creek bed before uprooting multiple large trees at a home site on Prince Lake. The tornado continued east northeast, snapping large limbs and knocking down a few trees as it crossed Old Gunter Rd and Mellyn St. About a half-dozen medium to large trees were uprooted at a home between Mellyn St and Mellwood Dr. The tornado lifted shortly after crossing Mellwood Dr.
Several trees were blown down around Fletcher.
Multiple trees were blown down onto roads and power lines on Connecticut Ave and North Church Street in Spartanburg.
Penny size hail was reported on highway 14 near highway 414.
Suber road was partially flooded by a stream near the Sweetbriar Court intersection. This is just upstream of the creek's confluence with the Enoree River.
Several trees were blown down on C E Stewart Rd.
A tree was blown down at Clifton-Glendale Rd and Calvert St, and another was blown down on Beacon Light Rd.
A few trees were blown down along Redland Rd near highway 14.
Cedar Rock Estate Road was covered by a foot of fast moving water by Lower Creek.

Cane Creek Road in the northeast part of the county was flooded. Water was reported over the road along 226 N in the northern part of the country. Sparks Road was reportedly flooded during the late afternoon. Heavy rain continued into the evening and overnight hours with more roads flooded as the event transitioned from a short fused flash flood event to one of duration flooding.
Numerous roads were reportedly closed across the county due to flooding, including Highway 70/25. Some roads were heavily damaged by flooding and landslides.
Two homes were damaged by flooded creeks in the Walnut community.

Numerous creeks went out of their banks with several roads closed throughout the county. This includes locations along the North Toe River and Mullin Hill Road in the Ingals area. Based on social media reports and hourly rainfall, the worst of the flooding began around 6 pm EDT.
Numerous roads were closed by flooding throughout the county during the late afternoon and evening hours.

The county communication center reported that Jackson Creek had flooded and closed Jackson Road near the intersection of Howard Gap Road. Etowah School Road was flooded by Gash Creek near the intersection of Drexel School Road. Also, Warlick Road was flooded by Boylston Creek not far from the intersection of Turnpike Road.
Brugg Street was flooded and closed by a small stream. A spotter in the Blacksburg area reported 4.10 inches of rain overnight.
Johns River Road was flooded by the Johns River.
A few trees were blown down, including one large tree, near Waterloo. Also, the roof of a porch was lifted from a home near Lake Greenwood.
A couple trees were blown down on Mauldin Rd.
A couple trees were blown down around Abbeville, including on Trail Drive and the Highway 28 bypass on the west side of town.
A tree was blown down on Rock Hill Road, about 5 miles northwest of Abbeville.
A tree was blown down on Wright School Rd and another in the same area on Bethany|Church Rd. Both locations are about 6.5 miles south of Belton.
A scattering of trees was blown down from about four miles southeast of Anderson up to Interstate 85.
Tree limbs were blown down in the Mooresville area.

Multiple trees were blown down from the Thicketty community, across Gaffney to the Blacksburg area. One large tree limb fell on and killed a 34-year old man standing in front of his house on 7th St in Gaffney.
Multiple trees were blown down across the southern part of the county.
Tunnel Road was flooded by a creek near Kenilworth Road. A spotter a little north of this location reported a 24 hour rainfall total of 3.94 inches.
Silversteen Road was washed out at the intersection of Diamond  Creek Road by the West Fork French Broad River.
Multiple trees were blown down from Polkville to Casar.

Several streets were flooded from the Biltmore Forest area northward to Asheville. Numerous roads were closed by flooding, landslides and fallen trees. Around 9 pm EDT a large debris flow took out part of Vance Gap Road, isolating several homes. Around a dozen residences had to be evacuated as a result of the slide.
A tree was blown down on Abington Rd near highway 90. Another tree was downed on Collettsville Rd in the same area.
Jay Clark Road was flooded by Saddle Creek. Pax Hill Road was closed in the Chesterfield community by flash flooding. Powerhouse Road near Bridgewater dam was also closed.

Globe Road was closed due to flash flooding along the Johns River. Anthony Creek Road off of Globe Road was flooded. Old Johns River Road and Wilson's Creek Road were closed due to flooding. The North Carolina Forestry Service evacuated over 100 people from Mortimer Campgrounds near Edgemont. Upper Playmore Beach Road was also closed due to flooding.

The Johns River crested at 16 feet between 4 and 6 am on the morning of the 5th. Flood stage is 12 feet. A few roads were closed near the river. The river was above flood stage until the middle part of the day on the 5th.
A large tree was blown down on Sam Turner Rd near highway 184. Highway Patrol reported another tree down nearby on highway 187, about 5 miles west of Iva.
A tree was blown down on Wingo Heights Rd, about 5 miles west northwest of Spartanburg.
A tree was blown down on Hanging Rock Rd near Boiling Springs.
Multiple trees were blown down from Conley Rd, about 5 miles west southwest of Morganton, across the Oak Hill community, to Henderson Mill Rd. Trees fell on a building on Henderson Mill.
Penny size hail was reported near the intersection of Goodman Lake Rd and highway 181.
A couple trees were blown down on highway 64 near Lake Lure.

White Pine Creek flooded Clark Creek Road about 4 miles south of Newland. Flooding was reported on Mount Pleasant Road at Crossnore Creek as well as along Millers Gap Road. The North Toe River crested about 1 foot above flood stage in Newland at 559 pm EDT.
Old Johns River Road was flooded by the Johns River.
Public reported that Brushy Creek was out of it's banks and damaging a road in the Kingsgate Subdivision. The bridge on Boiling Springs Road near Brushy Creek was completely submerged.

Guilder Creek flooded East Butler Road to a depth of about 3 feet. One car was caught in the flooding and the occupant had to be rescued. A mobile home park on Old Mill Road was flooded and the residents evacuated. Corn Road next to Mauldin High was flooded at the bridge. The bridge was damaged, closing the road for several weeks. At least 8 homes suffered significant flood damage in Mauldin. Ashemore Bridge Road was flooded and impassable about a mile southwest of Mauldin.

Pearman Dairy Road/SC28 flooded near Westside High School. A foot of water was flowing over the road with a car in a ditch at the intersection of Old Asbury Road and Whitehall Road (7 W Anderson). Flooding at the intersection of highway 24 and New Hope Road (6 W Anderson). A sink hole opened up on Hattons Ford Road during very heavy rain. Two utility trucks were damaged after driving into the hole which was about 3 feet deep and spanned the entire road (4.5 SE Townville). Indian Trail Road near highway 24 was flooded by a stream near highway 24.
Portions of Shackleburg Road were covered by water, especially around Jones Creek.
Sitton Shoals road was flooded by a stream.
Bond Kelley Road was flooded and closed by a stream.
Numerous trees were blown down in the Barnardsville area.

Several trees were knocked down between Waterloo and Laurens. Some trees were knocked down by strong winds, though most of them likely fell more a result of torrential rain and saturated soil. A tree fell on a home near Laurens.
Lightning started a fire at a 4000 square foot home that completely destroyed the structure.
A tree fell in saturated soil, possibly due to gusty winds, across highway 76. A vehicle later collided with the tree, killing the passenger.
Poplar Springs Road flooded, likely near Walnut Creek.
Todd Quarter Road was losed due to flooding at the bridge over Long Lick Branch.

Significant urban flooding developed, with several roads flooded across the northwest part of the city. Also, Sample Branch flooded Sample Road and flooded a home. The residents of the home were evacuated. A police cruiser was flooded at this location. Woodlawn Road was closed between highway 72 and highway 10 due to flooding along Big Curltail Creek. Four homes were evacuated in this same area in the Gatewood Community at Woodbridge Road.
Seneca Street in Calhoun Falls was flooded by a creek.
The Amity Lane bridge was washed out in the Trinity Farms neighborhood. The same location was damaged by an earlier flash flood at the end of June.
Public report of trees blown down near Bethlehem.

Brick Yard Road flooded along Beaverdam Creek. A mobile home was flooded up to the foundation in this area. Horse Farm Road was also flooded about a mile downstream from this location along Beaverdam Creek.
Flood waters from Beaverdam Creek covered portions of the Red Minnow Fish Lodge, located off of Brewers Bridge Road. Some mobile homes were flooded in this area as well.

Reems Creek Road was flooded by Reems Creek near where the road intersects with Many Branch and Sugar Cove Roads. After the creek subsided, a significant amount of debris was left on the road which had to be cleared by earth moving equipment causing the road to be closed for several hours. A couple nearby dirt roads were washed out, cutting off several houses.

Flooding along Beaverdam Creek washed out a private access bridge on Pinecroft Road. The road itself was also flooded. The Beaverdam Fire Department was flooded to a depth of 3 feet, causing damage to the station and taking it out of service. Three families in this area were temporarily relocated due to the flooding threat. Flowing water was 1.5 feet deep over the roadway at Weaverville Highway and Breckenridge Parkway. Merrimon Avenue was also flooded at Beaverdam Creek in this same area.
Sandy Mush Creek flooded, affecting Turner Cove Road and blocking two homes. Four other roads in this area, and toward Leicester, were also flooded.
Some homes were flooded along Stewart Creek with evacuations. Flooding was reported along Margaret Turner Road with water reportedly entering one home. Stewart Creek also flooded Southwest Blvd.
West Morehead Street was flooded and closed by Stewart Creek. Spruce, Merriman and Wilmore Streets were flooded in this same area, forcing some residents to evacuate.

Main Street and Church Streets were flooded in Fort Lawn. Water entered the  Fort Lawn Methodist Church and the Fort Lawn fire department. The church sustained significant flood damage. Reaves Creek also flooded Shirley Road just outside of town. A couple dirt roads in the area were also washed out, including Harbor House Drive near the Catawba River.
Stroud Road was washed out near the intersection of Richburg Road. Deer Branch Road at highway 21 was also flooded (5 N Great Falls) as were sections of highway 21 about 3 miles north of Great Falls.
Eaves Road was reportedly flooded and closed by a creek.
Times Drive was flooded and closed as was a portion of the Rice Avenue Extension on the west side of Union.

Mount Lebanon Road between Hully Bridge Road and Putnam Road was closed due to flooding. A road closure was reported at the intersection of West Springs Highway and Sulphur Springs Road (4 WSW Jonesville).  Dillard Road from Wildcat Road to the Spartanburg County line was closed due to flooding.
A culvert and part of a road were washed out on Sharpe Mill road.
Trees were blown down on power lines along highway 70 near Glen Alpine.
Public reported quarter size hail near Glen Alpine.
Quarter size hail near the intersection of highways 123 and 133.
A scattering of trees were blown down across central Greenville County including along North Parker Rd, Farmington Rd, as well as on Sweetbriar Rd. Also, a tree fell on a house in the Berea area.
A tree was blown down along highway 76 near highway 127 and another tree down near Country Club Place on the east side of Laurens.

Multiple trees were blown down across the central and western part of the county, from the north side of Rutherfordton, to between Forest City and Rutherfordton, to just south of Rutherfordton. One fallen tree ruptured a gas line on Oscar Justice Rd.
A tree and multiple large limbs were blown down off Hunt Rd.
Quarter size hail was reported in Easley.
Several roads were flooded in the Berea area.
A few trees were blown down from Tryon to the Green Creek community.
A tree was blown down on North Shamrock Ave in Landrum.
A tree was blown down on highway 9 near Meredith Rd.
Trees were blown down on Big Island Rd about 9 miles south southeast of Rutherfordton.
Multiple trees were blown down along highway 247.

Multiple large limbs and one power line were blown down in the Lyman area. Additional trees were blown down at Danzler Rd and highway 290 and at Danzler Rd and Duncan Reidville Rd. Trees were also blown down along Duncan Reidville Rd.
A tree and large limbs were blown down in the extreme southwest part of the county.
Hart Cut Rd was closed due to flooding. Pine Ridge Dr was also flooded and closed in this same area.
Widespread trees were blown down in the Collettsville area. Several roads were blocked by fallen trees. Trees also fell on a few homes.
One inch diameter hail was reported in and around Collettsville. Hail remained piled up in spots until the next day.

Highway 90 at Franklin Place flooded by Franklin Branch. Several other roads were reportedly flooded in the Collettsville area. Some roads were blocked by small landslides as well, including NC Highway 90 near Abington Road.
Half dollar size hail was reported in Lenoir.
At least four roads were closed around Calhoun Falls due to severe urban flooding.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down along Kathy Rd, eastward to Byrd Rd.
Half dollar size hail fell from Kathy Rd on the southwest side of Glen Alpine to Causby Rd.
Trees were blown down along I-40 near Old Fort.
Large hail fell on Jenkins Rd.

A stream flooded Houston Road near Dimsdale lane, trapping people in their cars (2 NNE Columbus). Two mudslides were also reported around Mill Spring.  A 40 foot section of Peniel Road was washed out by Mill Creek between Hugh Champion Road and Highway 9 south. A private road, Hawks Landing Drive, also had a large section washed out in this area. Water reportedly entered a few homes in this area as well.
A combination of gusty winds and extremely heavy rainfall caused a tree to fall on and destroy a home on East Main St.

Two people were trapped in their cars by a flooded creek on Cherry St Extension. A least one of the cars was swept into the stream. West Queen Street was Flooded by Eighteen Mile Creek (4 SSE Clemson). There was also considerable urban flooding in Pendleton with water entering a few businesses.

The Clemson Botanical Garden was heavily damaged by flash flooding. Damage to trails, bridges, and other infrastructure was estimated to total 200,000 dollars. Extensive damage was done to the garden's collection of rare plants, though it is difficult to estimate a dollar value for this loss.
Tokeena Road near Oakway was flooded by a stream.
Multiple trees were blown down near Lee Cemetery Rd, with additional trees down on Sardis Rd about 6 miles south of Union.
Several trees were blown down on Vaughn Rd.
High flows along a stream damaged a private access bridge.
Multiple trees were blown down in the Cane Creek area.
Numerous trees were blown down near Harmony.
Quarter size hail was reported 2 miles north of Harmony.
Trees were blown down on Emerald Woods Dr.
Quarter size hail fell in the Jonas Ridge area.
NWS Blacksburg, VA relayed a report of nickel size hail in Stony Point.
Multiple trees were blown down across the county, mainly northern sections, although a few trees were also down in Sherrills Ford. Interestingly, the storms this day moved from east to west.
Several small trees were blown down a little west of Huntersville.
Trees were blown down on power lines on Knobs Landing in Connelly Springs, on Morganton Furniture Rd (3.5 WSW Valdese) and in the Oak Hill community northwest of Morganton.
Multiple large trees were uprooted and some power lines were blown down in the Casar area.
Numerous trees were blown down in the northeast part of the county.
Multiple trees were blown down in the Ellenboro and Bostic areas.
Numerous trees were blown down in the Mooresboro area. Some trees fell on structures and power lines.
Multiple trees were blown down along highway 11.
A few trees were blown down between Rock Hill and Lake Wylie, with some trees on power lines.
Multiple trees and power lines were blown down, mainly across the northwest part of the county. Affected roads included State Line Rd, Green Lake Rd, Woods Farm Rd and Swofford Dr.

Numerous large limbs blown down and blocking roads in the Chesnee area. At least two trees fell on houses in Chesnee. Highway Patrol reported at least a dozen trees blown down from the Chesnee area, across Boiling Springs and north Spartanburg, to Reidville. NWS employee reported multiple trees and numerous large limbs down centered in the area near Blackstock Rd and Hidden Hill Rd.
Larger than golf ball sized hail fell along highway 290, south of Lake Robinson.

Multiple reports of downed trees were received from the public around Greer, mainly on the west and north side of town. Spotter reported numerous large limbs and power lines down in the Augusta St area just south of downtown Greenville. Highway Patrol reported more than  a dozen trees blown down from north of Greer, across Taylors and the Wade Hampton community to the downtown Greenville area.
Quarter size hail was reported west of Lyman.
Quite a few trees were blown down across the north and west part of the county from the Gray Court area, across Hickory Tavern and the Boyd Mill Pond area to near Ware Shoals.
NWS employee relayed report of quarter size hail near Lake Hartwell in the Sandy Springs community.
Numerous trees and large limbs were blown down throughout Abbeville County.
About a half dozen trees were blown down from the north side of Anderson west to Lake Hartwell.
About a half dozen trees were blown down, mostly across the central part of the county and the city of Greenwood.
Multiple trees were blown down in the Tiger area.
Numerous trees were blown down across the county. A tractor trailer truck ran into a  fallen tree on highway 123 about 5 E Toccoa.
Over a dozen large trees were blown down to the northwest of Clarkesville.
Multiple trees were blown down in the southwest part of the county, with several trees blocking roads.
Trees were blown down around North Shamrock Rd and Greenwood St.

East Howard Street was flooded by a tributary of Vaughn Creek. Also, water was reported to be swiftly moving across a low part of Landrum Road, likely due to a creek (5 SE Columbus). An NWS employee reported 4.35 inches of rain in this area in two hours (4 E Columbus).
Hooper Creek flooded Henderson Road, making it impassable to through traffic.
Two trees were blown down near downtown Waynesville.

Around 2 inches of rain fell in less than an hour, sending a small stream into 9  apartments in the Arcadian Village Apartment complex on Cedars East Court. The Red Cross sheltered 30 people whose apartments were damaged by the knee-deep flood waters. Also, McMullen Creek flooded portions of Addison Drive and Lincrest Place.
Central Road and Bishop Branch Roads flooded and closed.
Big Generostee Creek flooded and closed the Highway 28 bypass.
A low spot along Highway 24 near the intersection with Highway 11 reportedly had water moving swiftly across it, making it difficult for traffic to pass.
Urban flooding affected Shiloh road at the intersection of Davis Mill Road on the east side of Seneca.
Runoff from heavy rain caused deep ponding of water on Barrett Way near Choestoa Creek.
Apple Orchard Drive was flooded by a creek with water approaching a home.
More than a dozen trees were blown down at a golf course off Black Mountain Rd. Some power lines were also blown down and houses had shingles removed in the same area.
Several small trees were blown down in the Townville area.
A tree was blown down on Sue Cleveland School Rd near highway 86 in Piedmont with another tree blown down nearby on Woodmont School Rd near highway 86.
Multiple trees and power lines were blown down on White Pine Dr in the Glenwood community.
Several trees and power lines were blown down in the area around South Park Mall, with one tree on a house on Scofield Rd.
Penny size hail was reported at Tyvola Rd and Park Rd.
A tree was blown down on Hillbright Rd close to highway 72. Another tree was blown down nearby on Stringfellow Rd near highway 72.
Several Streets around Southpark Mall were flooded and closed during the late evening hours as a result of severe urban flooding, including the intersection of Fairview Road and Sharon Road.
A couple trees were blown down on power lines near Pioneer Mill Rd and Morrison Rd and several trees were blown down off Troutman Rd.
FD reported numerous trees blown down in the Lake Wylie/Steele Creek area.

A gas station canopy was lifted and blown on top of a vehicle on the southeast side of Shelby. Also, newspaper reported several trees blown down along Earl Rd in Patterson Springs and a tree on a home on Joe's Lake Rd.
Up to quarter size hail fell in the Jonas Ridge area, with at least one vehicle damaged.
About five trees were blown down in the Marion area.
Golf ball size hail fell in the Shingle Hollow community and quarter size hail in the Green Hill community.

Trees were blown down around Cove Creek Rd and Porter Rd. Additional trees were downed along highway 178 just north of town. Also, utility company reported multiple large oak trees down along highway 178 near Hagood Mill Rd.
Quarter size hail was reported off Gap Creek Rd.
National Severe Storms Lab relayed public report of nickel size hail on Devenger Rd.
More than a dozen trees were blown down from the east side of Greenville, across Mauldin and Five Forks.

Up to quarter size hail fell along the Roper Mountain Extension. The National Severe Storms Lab relayed a public report of quarter size hail off Miller Rd, 2 miles northeast of Mauldin. Also, a HAM radio operator reported quarter size hail on Barrett Rd near Mauldin.

The event started with several streets flooded in Hickory. Over the next couple hours numerous roads and even several homes were flooded in western Catawba County as extremely heavy rain continued to fall. In excess of 10 inches of rain was measured in this area.

Several streams were out of their banks and roads flooded in and around Conover. Flooding then became widespread across the central and northern part of the county. Several structures were damaged by the flood waters. A few roads were washed out|as well. til 10 am EDT.
Several roads were flooded in the northwest part of the county. Several swift water rescues were conducted. Some paved county roads completely washed out.

Widespread flash flooding continued across the central and northern part of the county. Several roads and structures were flooded. The Hickory Motor Speedway was completely flooded. Numerous swift water rescues were conducted in Newton and Conover. Several businesses in Conover and the east side of Hickory were flooded as were parts of the campus of Catwaba Valley Community College. As the flood crest begin to move downstream, flash flooding transitioned into a longer duration flood event during the afternoon.
Parts of Island Ford Road were flooded by streams between Old Mountain Road and Sharon School Road.

Several additional roads began to flood during the late morning hours over northwest Lincoln County as the flood crest worked downstream. Over 10 roads were closed by flooded streams. Road closures continued well into the afternoon hours.
Woodward Road closed by a flooded stream.

Widespread flash flooding continued across western Catawba County. As the flood crest moved downstream, flash flooding gradually transitioned into a longer duration flood event during the afternoon hours.
Forty sixth Ave Dr NE completely washed out. 10 feet deep trench where road was.
Buffalo Creek flooded Stroupe Road. Also, Brackett Road was flooded by Knob Creek (2 N Lawndale). Other roads remained flooded in the northeast part of the county.
At least two trees were blown down on Rollins Rd.

The public reported that Suber Road was flooded by Brushy Creek. Highway department reported that Mt Lebanon Church Road was closed due to flooding as was Jug Factory Road. Both Roads are about 6 miles north of Greer.
Twenty third Ave Pl between 4th and 5th street was flooded and closed by a tributary of Falling Creek.

Powerhouse Road was flooded. A tractor trailer and a number of cars were swept together by flood waters on Causby Road (1 S Glen Alpine). A swift water rescue was reported at Byrd and Conley Roads (5 SW Morganton). Jenkins Road was flooded near Burkemont Road (4 S Morganton). Swift water rescues were also reported along highway 70 and Kathy Road (3 SW Glen Alpine).

Despite no rain having fallen for several hours, A debris flow caused a large section of highway 194 to collapse, closing the three lane highway indefinitely. The event occurred around 11 pm at night just north of the intersection with Blevin Creek Road about 1 miles southeast of Elk Park. Two mobile homes and several vehicles were destroyed by the debris flow, though the occupants of the homes escaped unharmed.
Several large limbs were blown down on Johns River Rd.
Two trees were blown down on Laurel Lodge Rd near highway 197, with another tree down along highway 197 near the Habersham line.

Numerous roads remained flooded into the evening hours across central and western Catawba County. New flooding also developed as the flood crest moved further downstream along the South Fork Catawba and the Catawba Rivers.

Numerous roads remained flooded across the northwest part of Lincoln County into the evening hours. While the flooding then receded in the western part of the county, new flooding developed along the South Fork Catawba River and it's tributaries, lasting through much of the day on the 28th.

The South Fork Catwaba River went into flood starting during the early morning hours of the 28th. Several roads along the river flooded. Back water effects also flooded some roads along tributaries of the river. The river gauge at Lowell crested at 17.5 feet early on the 29th, the second highest crest at that location in over 70 years of gauge readings. Many streets along the river in downtown Cramerton were flooded. Water entered a few buildings, though sand bagging efforts prevented water from entering most structures.
Quarter size hail was reported in the Green Hill community.

Several trees were blown down in the Green Hill community. One large tree fell on a vehicle traveling along highway 64/74 near Green Hill, destroying the vehicle and causing serious injuries to the two occupants. The 66-year-old male driver died from his injuries several days later.
Multiple trees were blown down along highway 279.
Multiple trees and power lines were blown down along the highway 25/276 corridor from just south of Travelers Rest to the Furman area.
Up to quarter size hail was reported in the Walhalla area.
Up to quarter size hail fell near Fork Shoals.
A tree and power lines were blown down near the intersection of Nash Mill Rd and Tall Pines Rd.
Clamp Drive was flooded near Hencoop Creek.
Blake Dairy Road was flooded at Broad Mouth Creek.

A car was swept away by flood waters on Silver Creek Road. The car and it's occupant, a 23 year old male, were found separately downstream. The occupant was killed and the car destroyed. Two other cars were swept away at this location with 4 passengers rescued.

Urban flash flooding was reported on the east side of Seneca with many low areas filling with water. Water entered one home to a depth of a few inches in this area. also, several trees fell as a result of the heavy rain.

The Furman L Smith Memorial Highway was flooded over a 40 foot stretch near the intersection of Blue Bird Lane. Six Mile Creek flooded Jones Mill Road. The bridge over Jones Mill Creek was damaged and partially collapsed by flood borne debris.

Todd Creek Road was washed out near the Todd Creek Bridge. The road was damaged as water washed out a culvert under the road. Todd Creek also washed out Sunrise Road and flooded Browning Road in this same area. til 1230 am EDT.
A swift water rescue was conducted near the Pickens County flee market, near highway 183.
A home was flooded by Toms Creek along Turner Road. The occupants had to be rescued. Highway 17 was reported to be flooded near Eastanollee, especially around Ogg���s Branch.
Mt Olivet Road was flooded near Six Mile Creek.
The Green River Flooded Bobs Creek Road.

Several people were trapped by flood waters at the Whole Log Lumber Company along the Green River in the Zirconia community. They were taken to safety by a swift water rescue crew. About 3 feet of water swept through the facility, damaging lumber and equipment. A member of the public measured 6 inches of rain in Zirconia. Damage to area crops was also reported.
River Falls Road and Devils Fork Road were flooded by local streams.
Deep ponding of water was reported at Mauldin Street and Park Drive near Linley Park caused by poor drainage.
Numerous roads were closed due to flooding in the Cornelia, Baldwin, Alto and Mt Airy communities. Streams reportedly threatened homes, though there were no reports of significant damage.

Several trees were blown down on Semper Fidelis Rd, with one large tree on a house. In addition, a couple of outbuildings were damaged with tin roof material blown several hundred feet. Several trees were also blow down on Jennings Rd in the same area.
A few trees were blown down on Harmony Grove Rd.
Gusty thunderstorm winds caused the roof of a temporary stage to collapse as it was being erected at the Cleveland County fairgrounds.
Trees and power lines were blown down and blocking roads in the Springs Rd and Kool Park Rd area.
Multiple trees were blown down on power lines on Kyle Lane along the shores of Lake Norman. Another tree fell on a power line on Bluefield Rd, about 3.5 miles west northwest of Mooresville.
Multiple trees were blown down across the county.
Two trees were blown down near Edwards Rd and Talley Bridge Rd.
Quarter size hail was reported on the west side of Canton.
Multiple trees were blown down on the southwest side of the the Mills River community, including on Ray Hill Rd, Turnpike Rd and on Schoolhouse Rd.
Quarter size hail was reported about 2.5 miles north of St. Stephens.
Multiple trees were blown down on 4th St NW, with another tree down on 5th St NW.
Multiple trees were blown down along Warren C Coleman Bvd, mainly between Cumberland Ct and the highway 49 intersection.
A small tree and multiple large limbs were blown down along Anderson Mill Rd in the Roebuck area.
Two large trees were broken off and a third uprooted in the West Union community.
Multiple trees were blown down from Cana Rd near Angell Rd to Main Church Rd near highway 158.
Hail up to the size of pennies was reported in the Mill Spring community.

A cluster of slow moving and repeating thunderstorms produced 3.5 to 5 inches of rain in less than two hours near the Mecklenburg/ Union County line. Severe urban and small stream flooding occurred in the Matthews area, with water up to the windows of some vehicles. Stream flooding included a tributary of McAlpine Creek which flooded a part of Sam Newell Rd. Multiple roads were closed throughout the city.

Flash flooding developed along the Goose Creek basin when 3.5 to 5 inches of rain fell in less than two hours near the Union/Mecklenburg County line. A stream gauge on Stevens Mill Rd rose above the established flood stage around 630 pm EDT and crested more than 2 feet above flood stage shortly after 7 pm, flooding a portion of Stevens Mill Rd. The water moved rapidly downstream, with a stream gauge at Mill Grove Rd exceeding established flood stage shortly after 7 pm, also cresting more than 2 feet above flood stage around 830 pm.

Three to six inches of rain falling in a couple of hours caused an extreme urban flash flood and stream flooding event in the Greenville metro area. The flooding initially began on the east side of the city in the Haywood Rd/downtown airport area, where several cars were stalled in deep, rushing water due to an overflowing culvert on Byrdland Dr (3 E Downtown). A 39-year-old man and 36-year-old woman who abandoned their vehicles to seek higher ground drowned after being swept into the fast-moving water and nearby culvert which drained into Laurel Creek. A tributary of Richland Creek flooded several dozen apartment homes along Villa Rd between Pleasantburg Dr and Pelham Rd (2.5 ENE Downtown). The most severe flooding occurred on the east side of downtown, near the Stone Ave/I-385 intersection, due to a combination of Richland Creek overflowing its banks by several feet and major urban flooding. Multiple vehicles were stalled in high water in this area. The high water caused a gas leak and explosion at a restaurant on Stone Ave, causing significant damage to the exterior of the building. Richland Creek and the Reedy River overflowed their banks and flooded much of Cleveland Park, which remained closed for two days. This was the worst flooding along this portion of the Reedy in almost 10 years. Additionally, a small tributary of Langston Creek flooded the intersection of Langston Dr and Highway 276 (3 NNW Downtown). Finally, Rocky Creek, or a culvert draining into Rocky Creek overflowed along I-85 near the Pelham Rd exit (7 E Downtown), sending water over the southbound lane and forcing closure of the interstate for several hours.

A major flash flood event developed in the Greer and Taylors area when 3 to 6 inches of rain fell in only a couple of hours. The primary problem area was Brushy Creek, which produced its worst flooding in recent history. A stream gauge on Brushy Creek between Hudson Rd and East North St reached its highest level (13.4 ft) since August 1995 (Tropical Storm Jerry). Water entered multiple residences along Edwards Rd in Taylors. Brushy Creek also flooded portions of Boiling Springs Rd and adjacent side streets. In addition, a small tributary washed out a bridge on Memorial Dr Ext near Tryon St (1.5 NW Greer). Two vehicles drove into the resulting hole and each driver received minor injuries. Other small tributaries overflowed their banks throughout the Greer and Taylors area, flooding roads and some homes.

Although the torrential rainfall ended across the Greenville area by midnight, flooding continued in the Reedy River basin near downtown through the night. The stream gauge near Westfield St did not fall below the established flood stage until late morning on the 11th. The main impact was to Cleveland Park, which remained closed due to damage for two days after the flood water receded.

Although heavy rain ended by around midnight, excessive runoff flowing from Brushy Creek and other tributaries caused flooding to develop along the Enoree River during the early morning hours, continuing until late morning. Multiple roads were flooded along the river between Hammet Bridge Rd and Highway 14. This was the worst flooding along the Enoree since 2005, and among the worst since Tropical Storm Jerry in 1995.

NWS Storm Survey found a short path of a weak tornado that touched down just south of Wilkerson Way, just off Montford Cove Rd near the Rutherford County line. The tornado initially only snapped a few tree limbs and flattened a hedge. The tornado moved rapidly north/northeast, flattening a corn field at a farmstead near Wilkerson Way. A portion of the north facing roof of a barn was removed at this location, with material tossed upwards of a 100 yards to the north. Another small shed was moved off its foundation by about 8 feet and its roofing was blown off. The tornado continued just east of due north, destroying a carport at a business and tossing debris as much as 200 yards. Some heavy motors were also pushed over at this location and a piece of steel estimated at 70 pounds was flung about 50 feet. A small trailer was also moved and damaged by flying debris. Another open bed trailer was apparently flipped and severely damaged. The tornado proceeded north/ northeast from there, moving through the yard of a home, where numerous trees were blown down and branches snapped. A barn under construction at this location had scaffolding from inside the barn blown out in opposite directions from the north and south facing doors. The tornado continued to blow down numerous tall evergreen trees as it moved north/northeast before lifting just north of Crossings Dr.

Flash flooding developed for the second night in a row across northwest Union County, after 2 to 3 inches of rain fell in a short period of time on top of soil saturated from the 3 to 6 inches that fell on the evening of the 18th. In addition to urban flooding issues, the main stream affected was Goose Creek, where an official NWS stream on Highway 1524 far exceeded the estimated flood stage. In fact, the 13 feet reading was a record for this site. Fire dept reported multiple water rescues on flooded roads that included Red Lanter Rd, Briarwood Ct, Redwood Rd, and Indian Trail Fairview Rd.
Media reported a combination of gusty thunderstorm winds and saturated soil due to heavy rainfall caused a tree to fall on a house on Scaleybark Rd.

Although heavy rain ended in the Goose Creek basin by mid-evening of the 19th, continued runoff resulted in the stream remaining out of its banks and flooding several roads, including the intersection of Highways 218 and 601, until well after midnight.
Public reported via Social Media that lightning struck the chimney of a home on Taunton Dr. Debris from the chimney fell on and injured a man and caused damage to the roof and deck of the home.

Although heavy rain ended in the Crooked Creek basin by late evening of the 18th, the stream remained out of its banks until well after midnight, flooding several roads, especially at Ridge Rd, which was actually covered in water until daybreak of the 19th.
